---
NO AIP BLIND SPOT: every execution the independent observer recorded inside the
window AIP claims to have covered is present in AIP's signed evidence.
---
AIP recorded 2 execution(s) the third-party observer did not. This is not by
itself a defect: the observers are configured for different scopes, and the
third-party tracer starts and stops as a process of its own.
---
Scope difference (not a defect): the independent observer also recorded 938 failed
execve ATTEMPT(s) — a $PATH search producing ENOENT, for example. Nothing executed,
so AIP's scheduler tracepoint correctly does not report them and they are excluded
from the comparison above. auditd sees attempts; AIP sees executions.
---
This compares reported executions. It does not make the host kernel trustworthy:
a sufficiently privileged attacker may deceive both observers, and where both read
the same kernel mechanism, one gate blinds both.
